fundamental.headline: Mixed business, but cheap vs its history
fundamental.health: Sales up 11% over the last year, it keeps 34 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it carries meaningful debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying less than usual: its price vs sales is lower than 93% of the last 5 years. Compared with similar companies, adjusted for growth, it's priced about in line.
drivers: It is buying back shares, which grows each shareholder's slice.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Average business that looks cheap: cheap for a reason is possible; only for those willing to dig deeper. This is research, not personal advice.

timing.label: No rush
timing.text: The chart is still weak; a better entry would be a close back above the 50-day average ($239.38).

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 1% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 11% last year; 10%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 10% (3 years ago 3%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $10 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 25% (3 years ago 3%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $66.3B, up 11% from a year ago — about 1.5× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $18.8B, up 13% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 10%/yr over 3 years and 13%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 20% vs a 5-year range of 0–21% (median 16%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $36.6B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($35.1B buybacks + $1.5B dividends) = 20.8% of the company's market value. Share count down 14.7% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $16.02, up 3% in 90 days; 2 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $16.75, up 19% in 90 days; 1 analyst raised, 1 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By product, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Subscription and support 95% of sales, up 12%; Professional services and other 5% of sales, down 4%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +103% vs a year ago · $11.77 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 103% vs sales 11%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 7 quarters running, by growing margins (3% → 36%): analysts keep underestimating it.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 11% from a year ago, about as fast as two quarters ago (12%): steady demand.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $20 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 157% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 18× last year's profit (its lowest in 5 years).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Dec 2; analysts expect EPS of $3.45, up 6% from a year ago. It usually moves about 7% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 3% in 90 days (2 raised, 1 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
